S032_7_S_PREMISE_IS_HALF_RIGHT_AND_THE_R.so_the_CEILING_on_deleting_the_head_enti: not a major component of the TOKEN. Removing every byte the head reads -- which no exact algorithm can do -- buys 6.84% of the byte wall.

AND_YET_IT_IS_THE_MOST_EXPENSIVE_SINGLE_.reading: BOTH READINGS ARE TRUE AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. Per DISPATCH the head is the giant of the graph, 675.4 MB against 55.7 MB for the biggest MLP dispatch. Per TOKEN it is 6.84%, because the MLP runs its 55.7 MB one hundred and twenty-eight times. A ranking by dispatch cost and a ranking by token cost disagree, which is the same lesson as dispatch-count-is-not-time arriving on the byte axis.

S032_8_ANSWERED_BY_ARITHMETIC_BEFORE_BUI.the_question: WHY MUST FULL LOGITS BE MATERIALIZED?
S032_8_ANSWERED_BY_ARITHMETIC_BEFORE_BUI.plus_the_dispatch: one sample_argmax_f32 of 628, at the ~2.7 us per-dispatch cost measured in ACCELERATOR_DISPATCH_IS_NOT_THE_COST
S032_8_ANSWERED_BY_ARITHMETIC_BEFORE_BUI.SO_THE_ANSWER_IS_THAT_IT_COSTS_ALMOST_NO: fusing argmax into the head is a real graph-boundary deletion and it is worth three hundredths of a percent. The head's cost is READING 675 MB OF WEIGHTS, and argmax fusion does not touch a single one of those bytes. Building it first would have been optimizing the visible boundary rather than the expensive one -- the same error the dispatch ladder made.
S032_8_ANSWERED_BY_ARITHMETIC_BEFORE_BUI.WHAT_WOULD_ACTUALLY_PAY_IS_A_DIFFERENT_Q: S032 §7E, a mathematically safe rejection bound that lets the head skip rows. That attacks the 675 MB rather than the 2 MB, and it is EXACT rather than approximate if the bound is sound. It is tested in the next block and predicted to prune little -- see the prediction recorded there before the run.

WHAT_THIS_ATLAS_IS_NOT: IT IS NOT THE TIME COLUMN. Bytes are exact; the ms figures are bytes divided by ONE effective bandwidth (352.5 GB/s, the sealed token's own 9.879 GB / 28.0208 ms) and therefore assume every family moves its bytes at the same rate. They do not -- ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH measured a q4-native matvec at 161.9 GB/s against a dense arm at 426.4 on the same machine, a 2.6x spread -- so a family's ms here is a LOWER BOUND on its time and the ranking by BYTES is what this receipt claims.
no per-dispatch duration exists and none is claimed; Metal timestamp sampling is probed as supported and deliberately not encoded (crates/hawking-core/src/metal/mod.rs:704)

activation traffic, KV-cache reads and the DeltaNet state are EXCLUDED -- they are small against 9.87 GB of weights but they are not zero, and KV grows with context while every figure here is context-independent

the 628 graph's non-projection dispatches (rmsnorm, add_residual, the DeltaNet-specific four, the GQA-specific three, argmax) read activations and no weights, so they are absent from a WEIGHT-byte ranking by construction and are not thereby free
